To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rotamer and accessible volume approaches lead to the same prediction errors for the conformation of a spin label and that a more sophisticated treatment of the environment of the label will be needed to improve the prediction accuracy.

1. the accessible volume approach predicts the actual conformation of a spin label in a crystal structure with an accuracy of about 4 Å; 2. the rotamer approach predicts the actual conformations with an accuracy of 4 Å; and 3. the rotamer and accessible volume approach deliver the same distance predictions accuracy of about 2.9 Å.
the rotamer approach and accessible volume approach are equally accurate in predicting the conformations of spin-labelled side chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the analysis of the structure of spin-labelled biomolecules and with the development of new spin-labelled biomolecules for the investigation of biological processes.
the development and evaluation of in silico algorithms to predict the conformation of spin labels attached to amino acid side chains.
the prediction of the spin label conformation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rotamer approach and the accessible volume approach are equally accurate in predicting distances between spin labels in protein structures, but both approaches are not yet accurate enough for a detailed structural analysis of spin labelled proteins.
the accuracy of the rotamer approach is not worse than 4 Å and the accessible volume approach is not better than 4.5 Å.
the accuracy of the in silico spin labeling algorithms is not yet sufficient to be able to use the method to determine the structure of spin labelled side chains with atomic precision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the in silico methods for spin labelling are still in their infancy.
the rotamer approach is not able to correctly predict the conformation of a spin label in a protein.
the spin labels in the crystal structure of T21R1 can be predicted with a precision of 2.5 Å using either the accessible volume approach or the rotamer approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rotamer approach and the accessible volume approach are not competitive and that they should not be compared in terms of accuracy.
the rotamer library approach, although not very precise, is still a valuable tool to predict the spin label conformations in proteins.
the crystal structure of T21R1 azurin provides a challenging structural benchmark that can be used for testing the performance of in silico algorithms.
